did_you_know.text: The verse presents the Lord as King, enthroned above the cherubim, and connects his kingship with awe throughout the world: the nations tremble and the earth shakes.
The verse emphasizes the Lord’s greatness in Zion and his exaltation above all the nations, presenting Zion as a central place where his kingship is revealed.
The divine name is described as great and awesome, and the verse repeatedly declares, “Holy is he.” Holiness is therefore a central attribute in the psalm’s description of the Lord.
The Lord’s kingship is described as one that loves justice. He establishes fairness and acts in Jacob with justice and righteousness; therefore, his rule is presented as just and upright.
The people are called to exalt the Lord and bow before his “footstool”—an expression describing the place beneath a king’s feet and emphasizing his greatness.
Moses, Aaron, and Samuel are listed together as those who called on the Lord’s name, and the verse presents them as central figures in prayer and the worship of the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses, Aaron, and Samuel from a pillar of cloud. Alongside the divine speech, the verse notes that they kept his testimonies and followed his laws.
The verse describes the Lord as one who answers his servants and forgives their sins, but also takes vengeance on their deeds; thus, mercy and judgment appear together.
The psalm concludes with another call to exalt the Lord and bow before his holy mountain, followed by the summarizing declaration: “For the Lord our God is holy.”
